claims.text: 13 November 2008: DIA Talking Paper U-326-09 references 'the Director's meeting with Senator Reid on 13 November 2008'.
05 January 2009: Talking Paper U-326-09 (dated 02 January 2009) prepared for 'Senator Reid Visit to [DIA], 05 January 2009'.

15 May 2009: DIA Info Memo U-429-09 states the review of deliverables was requested 'during a 15 May 2009 meeting with you after your meeting with Senator Harry Reid'. Talking Paper U-973-09 dated 04 May 2009 prepared for 'Senator Reid Visit to Director, DIA'.

19 November 2009: DIA Read Ahead for 'DIA visit with Senator Harry Reid', 19 Nov 09, 1645, 'Capitol, Senate Visitor Center, SVC-217', attendees including DEPSECDEF. Purpose: to address Reid's SAP request and 'the quality and value of the products produced thus far under the current contract'.

connections.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
connections.note: AARO's official history places AAWSAP (2009-2012), also known as AATIP, directly downstream of Reid's direction and the resulting DIA appropriation, and records that on 24 June 2009 Reid wrote to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III asking that the programme be made a Special Access Program - a request Lynn declined on the recommendation of Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence James R. Clapper, Jr. Tier 2: AARO is an interested party in its own history.

sources.name: AARO, Historical Record Report Volume 1, 8 March 2024

connections.edgeLabel: $22M congressionally directed to DIA for advanced aerospace threat work
connections.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
connections.note: AARO's official history states: 'At the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats to the United States. In coordination with the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, DIA established AAWSAP in 2009... The contract for this DIA-managed program was awarded to a private sector organization.' AARO is an interested party in its own institutional history, which is why this is tier 2.

sources.name: AARO, The Department of Defense All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office Historical Record Report Volume 1, 8 March 2024

connections.edgeLabel: 24 June 2009 Reid SAP request refused by the Deputy Secretary
connections.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
connections.note: 'On 24 June 2009, Senator Reid sent a letter to then Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting that AAWSAP/AATIP be made a DoD Special Access Program. Deputy Secretary Lynn declined to do so based on the recommendation of then-Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, James R. Clapper, Jr., that such a designation was not justified.'
